topic: The Duality of Cross Products: From Geometry to Linear Transformations
target_audience: University students in Linear Algebra or Physics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The 2D Area Intuition
lecture_lines: Start with two vectors in two-dimensional space.
Their determinant represents the area of their parallelogram.
Cross products generalize this area intuition into 3D.
animations: Show vectors u (#FF5733) and v (#33FF57) starting at the origin in a 2D plane.
Animate ghostly copies of u and v moving to form a parallelogram (#FFFF33).
Fill the parallelogram (#FFFF33, 0.3 opacity) and display 'Area = |det(u, v)|' (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: Magnitude and Direction
lecture_lines: The cross product's magnitude equals the parallelogram's area.
The resulting vector is perpendicular to the inputs.
Use the right-hand rule to find the direction.
Point fingers from vector A towards vector B.
Your thumb reveals the cross product's orientation.
animations: Show two 3D-perspective vectors a (#FF5733) and b (#33FF57) from the origin.
Highlight a skewed yellow parallelogram (#FFFF33) on the plane of a and b.
Draw a right-hand graphic with fingers pointing along a and b to show orientation.
Animate the cross product vector a x b (#3357FF) growing perpendicularly from the plane.
Label the vector as |a x b| and show it equals the parallelogram area.

sections.title: The Linear Transformation Perspective
lecture_lines: Consider a transformation mapping space to a line.
It calculates the signed volume with a third vector.
This linear map corresponds to a dot product.
The cross product acts as the dual vector.
It bridges 3D volumes to 1D scalar outputs.
animations: Display the equation f(w) = det(u, v, w) in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Show a 2D-projected 3D grid and a test vector w (#FFFFFF) moving within it.
Transform the grid lines to collapse onto a 1D scalar line.
Highlight a vector (#3357FF) that represents the mapping of w to a scalar.
Label this vector the 'Dual Vector' which is the cross product u x v.

sections.title: The Determinant Formula: Why the Matrix Works
lecture_lines: The determinant formula calculates the cross product components.
These components are projected areas on coordinate planes.
Summing these projections defines the final vector.
animations: Display a 3x3 matrix determinant with top row unit vectors i, j, k.
Highlight the i-component and show a 2D projection on the YZ-plane area.
Highlight the j-component and show a 2D projection on the XZ-plane area.
Highlight the k-component and show a 2D projection on the XY-plane area.
Combine the three resulting components into the final cross product vector (#3357FF).

sections.title: Practical Application: The Mechanical Torque
lecture_lines: Torque represents the rotational effect of a force.
Maximum twist occurs when the force is perpendicular.
The cross product calculates this rotational efficiency.
animations: Show a bolt [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bolt.svg] (#888888) and wrench with position vector r (#FF5733) along the handle.
Apply a force vector F (#33FF57) at the wrench end at a 90-degree angle.
Animate the torque vector tau (#3357FF) pointing out and rotate the wrench around the bolt [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bolt.svg].

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: The cross product links geometry, algebra, and transformations.
It measures area, solves determinants, and maps space.
This unique duality defines its role in 3D.
It remains a fundamental tool in physics and math.
Visualizing these connections clarifies linear algebra.
animations: Show a 3-way split screen with a Parallelogram, Matrix, and Wrench.
Flash each panel in sequence (#3357FF highlight) to unify the different perspectives.
Fade everything out and display the final title: 'The Duality of Cross Products'.
